title: Comfort is the Killer of Creativity
description: Choe argues that comfort prevents artistic and personal growth, then demonstrates unstable spray-can control, deliberately creates difficulty and reminds viewers that paint can be revised rather than protected from every mistake.
summary: Choe argues that comfort prevents artistic and personal growth, then demonstrates unstable spray-can control, deliberately creates difficulty and reminds viewers that paint can be revised rather than protected from every mistake. This is an official-channel creative lesson or reflection, not clinical treatment or a universal formula. Its chronological map follows the route's own transcript and distinguishes art-making instructions from autobiographical claims, jokes and metaphors. Visually dependent technique still requires the source video.

chapters.title: It is only paint and can be revised
